subject.title: Add structured process events for sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core session-level process/step event contract now, and if so what taxonomy, persistence, replay, authorization, and redaction rules should it use?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested API becomes a durable gateway/session contract and can expose sensitive intermediate run state, so automation should not choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design core process events
options.body: Create a single additive gateway/session contract for process.* and step.* events with stable IDs, bounded replay, and explicit observer/redaction policy.

options.title: Narrow to progress consumers
options.body: Defer the broad process taxonomy and solve only one consumer first, such as inter-session progress or Control UI activity, without promising a general process ledger.

options.title: Reject core API for now
options.body: Keep existing lifecycle/item/tool streams as the only supported surface and ask integrations to use narrower existing events until maintainers sponsor a larger contract.

recommendation.title: Design core process events
recommendation.body: Create a single additive gateway/session contract for process.* and step.* events with stable IDs, bounded replay, and explicit observer/redaction policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-cutting history across agent events, gateway routing, sessions, and progress surfaces involved in this product/API choice.
